Subject: Intro + question on export sensitivity for Redwood inference purchase

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — SigmaMed is excited about the potential to speed up clinical-report generation. Procurement asked me to loop them in early because there are a couple of governance items on our side.

Two quick items:
1) The primary use will be on U.S. customers but SigmaMed ships internationally and we're subject to export control checks for certain dual-use analytics tools. Can you confirm whether any of the models or binaries we would receive are flagged as controlled tech?
2) We are also working through budget timing and would need a one-time partner-discount to meet our FY26 procurement window (~35% off list) — is that a possibility?

I've attached a zip with our corporate KYC packet and the product tech sheet for your security team to review. Happy to set a call if helpful.

Regards,
Kunal Singh
Head of IT Procurement
SigmaMed Solutions

Marissa

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal Desk export check — SigmaMed

Marissa — reviewed SigmaMed's techsheet and the KYC packet in the zip. Short summary:
- Nothing in the techsheet flags a clear ECCN class that would automatically require an export license from a U.S. perspective. The inference runtime is models + serving stack; we do not ship model weights or cryptographic modules that are on controlled lists.
- However, SigmaMed's international distribution footprint and potential installation in certain jurisdictions (they mentioned distributors in APAC) means we should run a restricted-entity check and KYC validation for end-users.

Requests before I can clear a formal attestation:
1) Confirm list of target countries/recipients for any deployments or reseller shipments.
2) Completed entity screening report for SigmaMed principals (sanctions, denied parties). The KYC zip had corporate docs but not the sanctions-screen snapshot.
3) A short SOW clause stating we will not ship model weights or tooling to third-party resellers without explicit export review.

If Procurement can provide the screening output (or give us permission to run it), I can issue a conditional attestation and suggested contract language by EOD tomorrow.

— Vivek
From: Kunal Singh <k.singh@sigmamed.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@sigmamed.com
Date: 2026-09-16T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal Desk export check — SigmaMed

Hi Marissa / Vivek,

Thanks for the quick review. Attached is an export-screening report our compliance team ran yesterday (excerpt included in SigmaMed_KYC_package.zip) and a short list of target countries: Canada, Germany, Japan, and authorized distributors in Singapore. No shipments to restricted jurisdictions.

We can agree to the SOW clause you mentioned: "Redwood will not provide model weights or exportable binary artifacts to third-party resellers without prior written export authorization." Procurement would like a statement they can submit to internal auditors that Redwood has reviewed and provided a conditional attestation.

Regarding the discount: procurement needs confirmation of approval to present to finance. Ideally we get written approval on the 35% one-time onboarding discount so PO can be raised this week.

Kunal

Subject: Approval: conditional discount + attestation for SigmaMed (RDW-2026-1972)

Team — after reviewing Vivek's notes and the updated screening from SigmaMed, I approve the following:

1) Commercial exception: one-time 35% onboarding discount for year-1 ARR only. This approval is contingent on the customer signing the attached SOW with the export restriction clause and acceptance of our standard MSA terms (no model-weight distribution).

2) Security attestation: Vivek to issue a conditional export attestation document stating: "Based on provided materials and entity screening, Redwood has no reason to believe the product qualify as ECCN-controlled; supply is approved for the listed jurisdictions (Canada, Germany, Japan, Singapore) subject to continued compliance checks."

3) Next steps: Laura, please prepare a Deal Desk approval memo and include the discount impact table and legal attestation. Rafael — coordinate DocuSign and procurement. Connor — prepare the VPC/restricted-deploy checklist for the onboarding runbook.

I will note in the approval memo that this is a one-off commercial concession and must not be considered precedent without VP-level re-approval.

Thanks — Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
